subject: Information Theory
title: Scale-Free Networks
description: A short lesson to help you apply Scale-Free Networks.

hook.text: On the web, a few sites have millions of links. Most have almost none. The distribution follows a power law.

buildup.text: Barabási discovered scale-free networks: the degree distribution follows P(k) ~ k⁻ᵧ. A few hubs dominate.

discovery.text: The mechanism is preferential attachment: new nodes connect to already popular nodes. Rich get richer.

twist.text: Scale-free networks are robust against random failures but fragile against targeted hub attacks.

climax.text: The internet, citation networks, and protein interactions all show scale-free properties. Hubs are everywhere.

punchline.text: Few hubs, many loners. Power laws shape all networks.

quiz.question: What is preferential attachment?
options: New nodes prefer connecting to already well-connected nodes
